benchmarks: custom 108-item dataset (68 software-engineering work items: 38 public GitHub issues + 30 authored; 40 real-estate listings: 20 public/collected + 20 authored), 3 independent runs on gpt-4o-mini + replication on 2 further base models incl. one cross-vendor; no public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Central mechanism: instance-channel leakage -- a learned correction bleeds onto unrelated same-domain Neutral items it should not affect (real-estate Neutral warm +0.353 vs Holdout-Sim +0.243), because retrieval treats every same-domain item as somewhat similar. Mitigated by human-governed consolidation: when corrections cluster (k>=3) an LLM drafts a rubric amendment, a human approves, both agents inherit it, and promoted exemplars are retired -- Neutral leak eliminated (7.73->8.12->7.72, back to baseline) while the learned lift is preserved. Separately, a canary/spot-check mechanism (10% of auto-accepts sampled, deterministic hash) guards against runaway learning: a deliberately injected bad lesson (canary phase X1, 'Long listings deserve top scores') was absorbed by 7-9/10 probe items and never flagged by the disagreement signal alone (small per-item increments stay within the agreement band); the spot-check is the explicit backstop for this poisoning-adjacent failure mode.

benchmarks: LongBench-v2-derived long-document benchmark (195 questions, custom-filtered for evidence breadth, RAG recall<=0.5) + custom multi-turn memory benchmark inspired by RealMem (120 dialogues, 24-49 turns, 5-9 key facts each)
fallos_mitigaciones: Central failure mode: passive top-K RAG retrieval discards relevant evidence BEFORE reasoning begins, especially when relevance is context-dependent/scattered across distant regions (Fig.1, Abstract) -- 'RAG stores context; it does not provide a memory system for managing, accessing, and reasoning over evidence.' Mitigated by full-fanout query-conditioned assessment (every sub-agent/region assessed, no early top-K exclusion) plus mid-agent shared regional coordination. Separately, Sec.4.3/Appendix E notes agentic sequential-compression baselines (Chain-of-Agents, MemAgent) 'can lose fine-grained evidence when answers require broad, non-adjacent support' -- an explicit competing-approach failure mode HMARS avoids by never discarding regions.

fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.9.2 Limitations, 'Contradiction resolution': the system automatically DETECTS contradictions (Sec.5.2, two semantically similar but opposing cells) but does NOT resolve them -- explicit unmitigated gap, resolution options (human arbitration, salience/recency-wins voting) left as future configurable choices. Sec.9.2 'Adversarial resilience': explicitly names a memory-poisoning risk -- 'a malicious agent could inject high-salience diffs to propagate misinformation' -- and proposes (but does not implement) trust scoring based on agent provenance/confirmation history as the needed mitigation. Sec.5.4 'Organic Knowledge Decay' is itself a staleness-handling mechanism: unaccessed cells decay via s(t)=s0*0.99^dt and stop propagating once below threshold, while a new decision superseding a stale one propagates through the region to inform affected agents.

benchmarks: custom Lewis signaling game (referential communication task, gpt-5.4-mini sender/receiver, 200 rounds x 3 studies, 8-object pool, capacity sweep |V|^L in {4..125}); no public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Study2 finding: stateless 'memory only' agents show a high-capacity collapse -- accuracy falls from 0.80(cap=25) to 0.52(cap=64) as collision rate hits 1.0 (every object's modal message collides with another's); the rolling 20-round window cannot accumulate enough evidence per code as the code space expands, and Study3 shows doubling the window (20->40 rounds) produces NO improvement at cap=64, confirming the failure is structural (no persistent carrier of conventions) not merely window-length. This collapse is avoided, not fixed, by switching to a persistent-notebook architecture (scratchpad), which keeps rising to 0.90 at cap=125. Separately, the codebook-meta condition's intended CONSOLIDACION mechanism fails outright: 'rather than developing structural insights... the note freezes by round 30 into generic operational reminders' and 'never becomes higher-order'; combined with the codebook's own lack of a pruning mechanism (stale/conflicting slot entries accumulate over 200 rounds), codebook-meta ends as the WORST private-memory condition (0.460+-0.14), explicitly 'worse than the simpler codebook it extends' -- an unmitigated design failure the paper reports as a negative result.

benchmarks: NINGUNO (single production workspace deployment: 73 memory files across 4 stores, 7 committed rows, one detect-verify-repair cycle; no public benchmark)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's entire subject is the 'stale-snapshot problem': persistent memory is a snapshot of the world at write time that does not update when the world moves, which is dangerous specifically for status-bearing claims ('not yet deposited','awaiting review','tool X is broken'). Documented incident (Sec.2, 2026-07-07): an agent's memory still asserted a paper was unpublished a day after it was published; caught only by consulting a machine-readable deposit ledger before acting. Three compounding root causes identified: (1) store fragmentation across project-scoped directories (a fact in one store invisible elsewhere), (2) a session-start guard comparing against the wrong (stale) index, firing unsatisfiable warnings that trained the user to ignore them (alert fatigue), (3) cross-agent staleness (a second agent's 12-day-old memory still described an already-repaired toolchain as broken). Mitigated by memgov v0.1.0: a SHARED_STATE commitment surface (rows overwritten in place with a verification anchor), a deterministic drift scanner producing a CONFLICT_MAP, a non-compensatory review queue (a flagged line can only be redeemed by verifying against its anchor, nothing auto-deleted), and a freshness heartbeat with governed friction (suppression markers to avoid retraining the alert-fatigue failure of root-cause 2). First scan: 73 files vs 7 committed rows -> 17 suspected drifts (confirmed true positives: 3 papers misremembered as unpublished, a repaired toolchain misremembered as broken) -> 14 remaining after verified repair.

benchmarks: custom PKPD model-selection benchmark (20 synthetic datasets) + PK parameter-recovery benchmark (20 profiles from 100,000 synthetic) + literature pipeline benchmark (17 cases: R01-R10 retrieval, E01-E05 extraction w/ 3 hallucination traps, S01-S02 synthesis) + real QSP case studies (Hall 2024 body-weight GLP-1RA, Gattoni cardiac electrophysiology, Kir atenolol PBPK, Shah & Betts mAb PBPK); baseline GitHub Copilot (GHCP); no public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Naive multi-agent context handling (full conversation-history concatenation) causes O(N x T) unbounded token growth and context degradation over long-horizon multi-session projects -- mitigated by capping every memory layer (scratchpad <=20,000/8,000 chars, decision log <=16,000 chars) and EVICTING completed work, keeping mid-term state bounded (median 301 tokens, max 4,050 across 104 runs) instead of growing with conversation length. Separately, hallucination-resistance is explicitly tested via adversarial 'trap' cases in the literature-extraction pipeline: an unretrievable PMID (HTTP404) -> system reports 'no records found' rather than fabricating model details (E01); two off-domain papers supplied -> correctly declined extraction (E02,E04); a mismatched-but-correct-paper PMID -> system detects the mismatch, autonomously locates the correct paper (E05). The PI Agent's mass-balance audit also autonomously DETECTED a mass-conservation inconsistency in a published paper's own parameter table (lung plasma flow exceeding summed peripheral-tissue flows) and imposed a flow-balancing constraint to restore conservation.
